headline: Three weeks of backlog cleared — and four benchmark scores that were never real

insights.title: The wrapper line held: 23 of 63 candidates rejected
insights.body: The highest-rejection cycle so far, and almost every rejection was the same shape — a paper improving a policy it never trains. Several said so outright: OnEvoMemory 'keeping the pretrained policy frozen', HyMeS 'no weight update, parameters remain fixed', Deltoris 'we do not train a separate small VLA model from scratch'. Titles are unreliable in both directions: FACT and EMS read like analysis and runtime papers but train real weights, while ARIES-Mission2 and RoboSynChallenge read like systems and are a frozen-model pipeline and a competition proposal.

insights.title: A RoboCasa #2 that was two other benchmarks misread
insights.body: StereoPolicy sat at RoboCasa 75.6 built from robocasa_toolhang_100: 94.1 and _200: 57.1. Its paper's Table 2 has no RoboCasa column at all — the row reads '941.9 ... 571.9', value and standard deviation run together, so 94.1 is Robomimic ToolHang @100 demos (94±1.9) and 57.1 is OmniGibson OpenDoor @200 (57±1.9). Two different benchmarks, two corrupted numbers. Fixed alongside three more: SimplerEnv averaged a paper's headline with its own sub-aggregates (TBD-VLA 82.09 → 77.7), COAST mixed three host policies, SAPS averaged in a pi0.5 baseline row.

insights.title: The tracker was discarding data it had already collected
insights.body: build_leaderboard.py filtered benchmark blocks through a hardcoded list of eight names, so 118 blocks across 91 models never reached leaderboard.json — including real_world for 59 models, which has its own definition file and appears in benchmarks_available. Meta-World was tracked by the data and absent from the dashboard, so nine models' scores were unreachable; it now has a chip and COAST leads at 94.0. Reviews for four models never attached because two scripts disagreed on filenames while coverage kept reporting 100%.

insights.title: 413 models; LIBERO's top-13 now spans one point
insights.body: G0.5 (Galaxea, single autoregressive stream) enters at #10 with 98.9 and also takes SimplerEnv at 87.3; LIRA follows at 98.88 from a 0.5B model running 186 Hz. The band from #1 to #13 is 99.8 down to 98.83. MiDAS was briefly the RoboCasa leader at 89.3 before that turned out to be RoboCasa-365 over three of four tasks — moved to its own block rather than ranked against the standard suite.
